name: Aveline Mourne
source_profile:
[p. 7] Duchess Aveline Mourne resorts to an unknown power during the siege of Castle Vesper. Her duchy and the invading northern army are destroyed. 4. 3E-990 — The death of the Unbending King

[p. 10] resulted in the abandonment of its principal settlements and the disappearance of its ruling family. Before the war, Duskfell was one of the ancient southern duchies of Cador, ruled for centuries by House Mourne. Its lands were dominated by rugged hills, ancient woodlands, fertile valleys, and fortified settlements guarding important approaches to the royal heartland. Although less wealthy than the Duchy of Cade or Valemont, Duskfell enjoyed considerable prestige owing to its ancient lineage and military traditions. Its ruling lady, Duchess Aveline Mourne, was a proud and formidable aristocrat who maintained close ties to the southern knightly orders. House Mourne had long defended the kingdom's interior approaches, and its ancestral stronghold, Castle Vesper, guarded an important road toward Cade. This made the duchy a natural target for northern armies seeking to force the crown into negotiations.

[p. 10] Duchess Aveline Mourne was the last recognized ruler of Duskfell. After the Silence of Duskfell, she disappeared and her ultimate fate remains unknown to all. Since then, the lands of Duskfell have fallen into ruin. The crown has never successfully established another ruling house there, and much of the territory remains effectively unclaimed. Political tension: The absence of a recognized ruler creates a peculiar legal situation. Several southern families may possess distant hereditary claims to the duchy, but none has successfully asserted authority over its lands. Some nobles might argue that Duskfell should be formally dissolved and its territory distributed among neighboring lordships. Others consider such a move an affront to the sanctity of hereditary titles.
